title: Lamport Timestamp Trap: Ordered Numbers Aren't Causality in a Balanced Search Tree
topic: The Lamport Timestamp Trap: Ordered Numbers Aren t Causality
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We investigate the Lamport timestamp trap, where ordered numbers do not imply causal order, in the context of a balanced search tree implemented in Chronos-Interpreter. The study formalizes the invariant that Lamport timestamps provide only a total order, not a partial causal order, and demonstrates how this property can lead to subtle bugs in distributed indexing. We present a lightweight Chronos-Interpreter implementation that augments each node with a Lamport clock and prove that the tree maintains strict height balance and key ordering while preserving the timestamp invariant. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V74 80-core system with 1 core and 2 threads shows a mean latency of 51635.39 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 19 367 ops/s over 30 iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261104_140125_the_lamport_timestamp_trap__or}
